title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: RHONDA'S EMPTY NEST
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Rhonda Gaines, a tugboat captain in Savannah, Georgia.
She pushes giant cargo ships into port all day.
But this fall, the hardest thing to steer was her own empty house.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE KEYS
segments.quote: A ship in harbor is safe, but that is not what ships are built for.
segments.author: John A. Shedd
lines: Her only daughter, Kayla, was driving to college in California.
Rhonda held the car keys a little too long.
Then she saw the old sign over her wheelhouse door, from the writer John A. Shedd:
A ship in harbor is safe, but that is not what ships are built for.
She let go, and waved until the car was a dot.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE PHOTO ALBUMS
segments.quote: Life can only be understood backwards; but it must be lived forwards.
segments.author: Soren Kierkegaard
lines: The house got very quiet. Every evening, Rhonda sat with old photo albums.
She cried at a picture of a birthday cake. Not even a good cake.
Her deckhand Luther texted her a line from the Danish thinker Soren Kierkegaard:
Life can only be understood backwards; but it must be lived forwards.
So she closed the album. What did she want next? Salsa dancing.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE PARKING LOT
segments.quote: It is hard to fail, but it is worse never to have tried to succeed.
segments.author: Theodore Roosevelt
lines: The VFW hall had a flyer. Salsa night, Thursdays at seven.
Rhonda drove there three times and never left her truck.
Then she remembered a line from Theodore Roosevelt:
It is hard to fail, but it is worse never to have tried to succeed.
On the fourth Thursday, she walked right in.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE DANCE FLOOR
segments.quote: The only way to make sense out of change is to plunge into it, move with it, and join the dance.
segments.author: Alan Watts
lines: Rhonda was terrible. She counted out loud and stepped on everybody's feet.
Her teacher, Mr. Ernesto, seventy-one, just smiled and quoted the philosopher Alan Watts:
The only way to make sense out of change is to plunge into it, move with it, and join the dance.
So she stopped counting and started moving. She still stepped on feet. But only his.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE PHONE CALL
segments.quote: Children have never been very good at listening to their elders, but they have never failed to imitate them.
segments.author: James Baldwin
lines: In October, Kayla called, crying. She failed her first chemistry test and wanted to quit.
Rhonda was ready with a big speech. Then she thought of the writer James Baldwin:
Children have never been very good at listening to their elders, but they have never failed to imitate them.
So, no speech. She told Kayla how bad she was at salsa, and how she kept going back.
Kayla laughed, and joined a study group.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: EVERY THURSDAY
segments.quote: Begin at once to live, and count each separate day as a separate life.
segments.author: Seneca
lines: At Thanksgiving, Kayla came home with a B and a new friend.
Rhonda always saved her happiness for holidays, like the good china.
Luther had one more line, from the Roman thinker Seneca:
Begin at once to live, and count each separate day as a separate life.
So now every Thursday is a holiday. And after the pie, she taught both girls to salsa in the kitchen.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Let them sail. Live forward. Try anyway. Join the dance. Show, don't tell. Live today.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Let them sail. Live forward. Try anyway. Join the dance. Show, don't tell. Live today.
I tried salsa once. The floor is still recovering.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
